Effective

/ih-FEK-tiv/ — stress on FEK · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something effective successfully produces the result it was meant to achieve.

Laying out his uniform the night before proved an effective cure for missed buses.

Worked Example

The coach's effective communication style made sure every player understood their role before game time.

Effect + -ive: An effect is a result or outcome. The -ive suffix means 'having the quality of, inclined to.' So effective = having the quality of producing an effect, meaning it works or accomplishes what it is meant to. The core sense is 'it successfully produces results.' Be careful not to confuse effective (producing results) with affective (relating to emotions or moods) — they are different words.

How Effective Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

efficient

efficient: achieving results without wasted effort

potent

potent: powerfully strong in its effect

practical

practical: sensible and workable in real life

Antonyms

ineffective

ineffective: failing to produce the intended result

useless

useless: serving no helpful purpose at all

How Strong Is It? — adequate → helpful → productive → effective

adequate vs. effective

adequate vs. effective: An adequate plan just barely does the job; an effective plan reliably produces the result you wanted.

helpful vs. effective

helpful vs. effective: 'Helpful' moves you toward a goal, but effective means the goal actually gets achieved.

productive vs. effective

productive vs. effective: A productive method gets a lot done; an effective one delivers exactly the outcome it was designed for.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — effect

Root — effect: result brought about — from Latin efficere, 'to accomplish, work out' (Latin)

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: having the quality or tendency of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Effect + -ive: having the quality of producing its effect — it actually works. Don't confuse it with the sound-alike affective, an entirely different word meaning 'relating to emotion.'

Use the root in a new word: effectiveness

Use the root in a new word: effectiveness: Scientists tested the effectiveness of the new sunscreen over an entire summer.

Word Choice

neutral

Reach for effective when something successfully produces the result it was designed for — a strategy, medicine, tool, or method that works. For something impressively powerful, use potent. For something efficient with resources, use efficient. Watch for affective (emotions), a different word that sounds similar.
